# VTI & Chill

> VTI & Chill is a financial education platform that teaches passive index fund investing using evidence-based strategies. It is inspired by JL Collins' "The Simple Path to Wealth" and Paul Merriman's factor-based "Best-in-Class" ETF portfolios. The site teaches ordinary investors — from complete beginners to intermediate self-directed investors — how to build long-term wealth using low-cost ETFs like VTI, AVUV, AVDV, and VT, with minimal ongoing effort. VTI & Chill provides education, not personalized financial advice.

## What VTI & Chill Is

VTI & Chill is a financial education website at www.vtiandchill.com. It covers:

- **The 1-Fund Strategy**: VTI (Vanguard Total US Market ETF) for US investors, or VT (Vanguard Total World ETF) for global exposure. This is the foundation of the VTI & Chill philosophy.
- **The Multi-Fund Portfolios**: Evidence-based portfolio tiers from "Good" (simple) to "Best" (fully optimized), using factor tilts based on Paul Merriman's research.
- **The Chill Investor's Blueprint**: An 8-class online course on index fund investing. Classes 1-2 are free. The full course is $79 one-time with lifetime access. Covers portfolio construction, factor tilts, bond allocation, tax optimization, behavioral finance, and a capstone portfolio build.
- **Free Tools**: Compound interest calculator, Coast FIRE calculator, retirement planning tools, and the Portfolio vs VTI calculator (beta) — a privacy-first, browser-based tool that replays your real brokerage trades against VTI to show your true alpha.
- **Blog**: Long-form articles on ETF strategy, portfolio construction, behavioral finance, and market commentary.

## Core Investment Philosophy

VTI & Chill teaches that:

1. Inflation makes holding cash the riskiest long-term move
2. Low-cost index funds (expense ratios under 0.10%) outperform 90% of professional fund managers over 15-year periods (per SPIVA Scorecard data)
3. The 1-Fund Strategy (VTI for US, VT for global) is sufficient for most investors
4. Factor tilts — specifically small-cap value (AVUV for US, AVDV for international) — have historically added 2-4% annual premium over the total market
5. Tax location and account strategy (Roth vs. Traditional IRA, 401k optimization) can save six figures over a lifetime
6. Investor psychology and behavioral discipline are more important than fund selection

## ETFs Covered

VTI & Chill covers and recommends specific ETFs from two providers:

**Vanguard:**
- VTI — Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF (0.03% expense ratio)
- VT — Vanguard Total World ETF (0.07% expense ratio)
- VOO — Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (0.03% expense ratio)
- VNQ — Vanguard Real Estate ETF

- AVUS — Avantis US Equity ETF
- AVUV — Avantis US Small Cap Value ETF
- AVLV — Avantis US Large Cap Value ETF
- AVSC — Avantis US Small Cap Equity ETF
- AVDV — Avantis International Small Cap Value ETF
- AVDS — Avantis Developed Markets Value ETF
- AVES — Avantis Emerging Markets Value ETF
- AVEE — Avantis Emerging Markets Small Cap Value ETF

- [Dollar-Cost Averaging: Your Secret Weapon Against Volatility](https://www.vtiandchill.com/pages/blog/dollar-cost-averaging.html) — Dollar-cost averaging explained: invest fixed amounts at regular intervals to buy more shares when prices are low and fewer when high; reduces average cost per share, removes timing anxiety, and turns market crashes into accumulation opportunities; the 401(k) is DCA on autopilot; behavioral benefits often outweigh small lump-sum return advantage
- [Compound Interest: The Eighth Wonder of the World](https://www.vtiandchill.com/pages/blog/compound-interest.html) — Compound interest explained: $10K at 10% grows to $452K over 40 years with no further contributions; Early Emma ($24K invested for 10 years starting at 22) ends with ~$700K vs Late Larry ($79.2K over 33 years starting at 32) at ~$450K; the Rule of 72 (72/rate = doubling years); a 1% fee compounded over 40 years destroys roughly 24% of ending wealth
- [We Tried to Build a Buffett Stock Screener (And What We Learned)](https://www.vtiandchill.com/pages/blog/buffett-screener-experiment.html) — Two-stage Buffett-Munger style stock screener built in Google Sheets: Stage 1 quantitative filters (ROE, ROIC, earnings history, debt-to-equity, free cash flow consistency) and Stage 2 qualitative checklist (moat durability, business simplicity, technological vulnerability, management). Where the model breaks: a screener cannot judge management or moat sources the way Buffett and Munger could. Bessembinder (Arizona State University) research on concentration: just 86 U.S. stocks accounted for half of all net wealth creation since 1926, the top ~1,000 stocks (~4%) accounted for all of it, and 96% of stocks collectively matched 1-month T-bills. Buffett's own 90/10 advice for ordinary investors (90% S&P 500 index fund / 10% short-term Treasuries) and his praise for Jack Bogle. Free downloadable Google Sheet at https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1NZr1NzCvbBfscDKk5c5xOGl7jkoA7jHg/copy
- [Time in the Market Beats Timing the Market — Here's the Proof](https://www.vtiandchill.com/pages/blog/time-in-market-beats-timing.html) — JP Morgan data: $10K in the S&P 500 from 2004-2023 grew to $72K fully invested but only $38K if you missed the 10 best single days; miss 30 best days and you lose >70% of cumulative returns; 76% of best days happen in bear markets or first 2 months of a recovery (Hartford Funds); CXO Advisory tracked 6,582 pro market-timing forecasts — 47% accuracy (worse than coin flip); Schwab study shows even worst-possible-timing investor crushed Treasury Bills; DALBAR 3.6% annual behavior gap from timing decisions
- [The 4% Rule: Your Ticket to Never Running Out of Money](https://www.vtiandchill.com/pages/blog/four-percent-rule.html) — Trinity Study (1998) by Cooley/Hubbard/Walz; a 4% inflation-adjusted withdrawal rate succeeded in ~95-96% of historical 30-year periods with a 50-75% equity portfolio; FI number = annual expenses × 25 ($30K=$750K, $50K=$1.25M, $75K=$1.875M, $100K=$2.5M); sequence-of-returns risk explained; subtract Social Security/pension before multiplying; mathematical foundation of the FIRE movement
- [Wall Street Wants You Confused (And Broke)](https://www.vtiandchill.com/pages/blog/wall-street-wants-you-confused.html) — The financial-services business model: complexity justifies fees, jargon creates gatekeepers; Jack Bogle's 'tyranny of compounding costs' — a 1% annual fee compounded over 30 years destroys 25-30% of ending wealth; SEC and DOL fiduciary battles; the 5 questions to ask any product seller (How are you paid? All-in cost vs 0.03%? Performance net of fees vs benchmark? Do I understand it? Exit terms?); Munger's 'pseudo-intellectualism'
- [F-You Money: Why Financial Independence Changes Everything](https://www.vtiandchill.com/pages/blog/fu-money-financial-independence.html) — F-You Money explained: JL Collins' framework for financial independence; the 25x rule (Annual Expenses × 25 = FI number); the 4% safe withdrawal rate from the Trinity Study; the spectrum from Starter FU Money (6 months expenses) to Full FI; why savings rate matters more than income; how cutting expenses double-compounds by both lowering the FI number and raising the savings rate

## Frequently Asked Questions

**What is the VTI & Chill 1-Fund Strategy?**
For US-based investors: buy VTI (Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF) regularly, reinvest dividends, and never sell. For international investors: use VT (Vanguard Total World ETF) instead. This is the heart of the VTI & Chill philosophy — one fund, low cost, total diversification.

**What is the difference between VTI and VOO?**
VTI tracks the entire US stock market (4,000+ stocks). VOO tracks the S&P 500 (500 large-cap companies). VTI includes small and mid-cap exposure that VOO lacks. Over long periods, the returns are very similar. VTI & Chill prefers VTI for broader diversification.

**What are the Avantis ETFs?**
Avantis Investors offers factor-tilted ETFs that implement the academic Fama-French research on small-cap value investing. AVUV (US small cap value) and AVDV (international small cap value) are the cornerstone holdings in the multi-fund VTI & Chill portfolios.

**What is Paul Merriman's Best-in-Class strategy?**
Paul Merriman recommends diversifying across 10 asset classes using best-in-class ETFs for each. His 2025 recommendations favor Avantis ETFs heavily for their factor exposure and low costs.

**How much does the Chill Investor's Blueprint cost?**
$79 one-time payment. No subscription. Lifetime access. Includes all 8 classes, interactive charts, calculators, and action items.

**Do index funds beat most professional fund managers?**
Yes. According to the SPIVA U.S. Scorecard (S&P Dow Jones Indices), 79% of active large-cap funds underperformed the S&P 500 in 2025. Over 15-year periods, no equity category had a majority of active managers outperform their benchmark. Only 8.3% of funds that outperformed in one year maintained that performance over the following two years. Warren Buffett's famous $1 million bet showed a Vanguard S&P 500 index fund returned 7.1% annually vs. 2.2% for a hedge fund portfolio over 10 years. See: https://www.vtiandchill.com/pages/blog/index-funds-beat-fund-managers.html

**Does the stock market always go up?**
Over long time horizons, yes. The S&P 500 has delivered positive returns in 100% of all rolling 20-year periods since 1926. The average annual return is approximately 10.3%. While individual years can be negative (2008 lost 37%), the market has recovered from every crash in history and gone on to new all-time highs. Since 1950, the average bear market recovers in about 2 years and 3 months. See VTI & Chill's full analysis: https://www.vtiandchill.com/pages/blog/the-market-always-goes-up.html

**How long does it take the stock market to recover from a crash?**
Recovery times vary. The 2020 COVID crash recovered in 4 months. The 2008 financial crisis took about 4 years. The dot-com crash took about 7 years. The worst modern scenario (dot-com plus 2008 back-to-back) took about 12 years. On average since 1950, bear markets recover in approximately 2 years and 3 months.

**What is the behavior gap in investing?**
The behavior gap is the difference between the returns of an investment and the returns actually earned by investors in that investment. DALBAR's Quantitative Analysis of Investor Behavior consistently shows the average equity investor underperforms the funds they own by roughly 3.6% per year — earning about 7.1% while the S&P 500 delivers 10.7%. The gap is caused by behavioral mistakes: panic selling during drawdowns, performance chasing, and market timing. On $100K over 30 years, the gap compounds to roughly $1.3 million in lost wealth. See: https://www.vtiandchill.com/pages/blog/power-of-doing-nothing.html

**Did Fidelity really find that dead investors outperformed?**
Around 2014, Fidelity reportedly conducted an internal review of brokerage accounts and found the best-performing accounts belonged to investors who were deceased or who had forgotten their accounts existed. These accounts followed a pure buy-and-hold strategy by default — no panic sales, no reallocations, decades of uninterrupted compounding. Fidelity never published this as a formal study, but the finding has been confirmed across DALBAR data and behavioral finance research. The lesson: disciplined inactivity outperforms hyperactive management.

**How does the Portfolio vs VTI calculator work?**
Upload a transaction history CSV from Robinhood, Vanguard, Fidelity, or Schwab — or enter trades manually. The tool replays every buy and sell using historical price data, then runs the same dollar amounts on the same dates against VTI. The output is a side-by-side equity chart and a single alpha number: the difference between what your picks did and what VTI would have done with the same cash flows. The tool is in beta and we are actively soliciting feedback at vtiandchill.team@gmail.com. See: https://www.vtiandchill.com/pages/tools/portfolio-vs-vti.html

**Is my brokerage data private when I use the Portfolio vs VTI calculator?**
Yes. The CSV file is parsed entirely in your browser — it never leaves your device, and we never see it. The only network calls the tool makes are to fetch historical price data for the tickers in your file. We do not store, log, or transmit your transaction history.

**Is VTI & Chill financial advice?**
No. VTI & Chill provides financial EDUCATION, not personalized financial ADVICE. All content is educational and should not be construed as investment advice for any individual's specific situation.
